Looking at the cuboid (4×2×2), I can track the visible cubes of each colour:

- **Light grey:** occupies the top-left corner region (three cubes in an L on top plus one below).
- **Black:** occupies the top-right back region (a zigzag of four cubes).
- **Medium grey:** occupies the bottom-right front region (three visible cubes plus one hidden cube at the back).
- **White:** visible at the front bottom (position 2) and top back (position 2).

The only hidden cubes are the three bottom-back cubes. The medium grey piece needs the hidden cube next to its front part, leaving the other two hidden cubes for the white piece. So the white piece consists of: a central cube (bottom-back, position 2) with one cube in front of it, one cube to its left, and one cube on top of it — a "corner" piece with three mutually perpendicular arms.

Checking the options (allowing rotation): only diagram C shows this three-armed corner shape in the correct handedness (a 180° rotation about the horizontal axis turns the white piece into diagram C). The other options are zigzag paths (A, B, E) or a flat T-shape (D).

\boxed{C}
